intelligence.human_view: The failure was not slowness — the work itself often took twenty minutes. The failure was the gap between done and shown, and between started and finished. A finished round that sits is invisible to the only judge who matters, so it earns nothing and teaches nothing; a started round that waits on another lane is not "in progress", it is parked, and parking is silent. Serial chaining made one lane's failure everyone's failure: the machine had one road and it was blocked. The law fixes the shape, not the effort: parallel lanes so no single failure blocks the machine, auto-triggers so the next step never waits on a human remembering, a one-hour timer so sitting has a deadline and a name, and done defined as his eyes, not our records. The floor-watch is the enforcement because memory is not enforcement — the night proved that twice over, once when the probe sat seven hours and once when the board's owed render was believed updated and was not.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you build a beautiful tower and then you hide it in a cupboard and never show anyone! That's silly, right? The rule is: when you finish something, you SHOW it right away — within one hour! And you never leave a job half-done while you go play somewhere else. Every job gets a little timer, and if the timer rings and nobody showed the work, the machine shouts about it! That way nothing ever sits in the cupboard again.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like baking a lovely cake and leaving it in the oven all day, love — nobody gets to taste it, and by the time you remember it's stale. The new rule is simple: when the cake is done, it comes straight to the table. Every job has its own little timer now, love — one hour — and if the hour passes with nothing shown, the machine itself tells him. No more good work sitting unseen while he waits.
intelligence.naya_view: I never let finished work sit. The moment a maker finishes, the checker is already named and going. The moment a round lands, it is either in front of his eyes or its next step is already dispatched — in the same pass, never later. Every owed thing carries its hour, and the floor-watch counts it down. Done means he has seen it. Anything else is sitting, and sitting is the failure the law was written for.
